thread:
devon: Heads up — p95 on /v1/chat jumped from 210ms → 360ms after last kernel switch. Looks correlated with larger microbatches and KV cache miss rate :thinking:

maria: Ugh. Did the canary switch change kernel prefetch heuristics?

devon: Yes, we swapped to kernel-v2.1 on canaries at 10:12. Here's a quick profile dump:
```
route=/v1/chat
kernel=kernel-v2.1
microbatch_mean_tokens=42
p95_latency_ms=360
kv_cache_hit=0.78 -> dropped from 0.92
batch_size_mean=7.8
```

anita: kv hit drop is big. Could be token-budget stretching batches across contexts, evicting useful KV too early.

ryan: Any change to queue policy? We recently relaxed early-cutoff to favor throughput.

devon: Yes, queue policy changed: `early_cutoff=off`, `token_budget_target=adaptive_by_tier`. That produced fewer, bigger batches for low-tier routes.

perf-bot: [perf/regression] p95 increase @3831234600 — investigated by devon

maria: If batches are larger, kernel-v2.1's prefetch might be oversubscribing device memory and causing paging that hurts kv locality.

sre-jen: Can we repro on a perf canary with kernel-v2.1 + old queue policy? If yes, we should rollback policy change and isolate variable.

devon: On it — will spin canary with `token_budget_target=static:20` and `early_cutoff=on` and run the synthetic workload (chat_short + long_context mix). ETA 45m :clock1:

anita: Also add a run with kernel-v1.9 + adaptive budget so we know which axis matters.

ryan: Action items: 1) devon run the two canaries and post aggregated traces. 2) perf-bot to chart kv_cache_hit vs batch_size across routes. 3) If kv hit <0.85 on /v1/chat, auto-scale token_budget_target down for that tier.

devon: Will post results in this thread. If we see the kv hit recovery with static smaller token budgets, we can tune adaptive gating thresholds rather than rollback kernel.

maria: thanks — definitely prioritize p95 on customer-facing routes. :white_check_mark:
